evidence.section: Effect of process on tensile property
evidence.quote: because of solid solution strengthening and precipitate strengthenin g resulting from the addition of Nb element, the yield strength and ultimate strength of the NiAl-Fe (Nb) alloy are much higher than that of the Ni-20Al-30Fe-Y alloy[11] at the same processing and testing condition.

evidence.section: Effect of process on tensile property
evidence.quote: This is because the microstructure of the DS NiAl-Fe(Nb) alloy is regular, and the microstructure is that the brittle β phase is surrounded by γ/γ′ phase, which is analogous to the cladding of extrud ing process, therefore large elongation is obtained.

evidence.section: Effect of process on tensile property
evidence.quote: Because the micro-defect was eliminated after the HIP treatment, the strength and ductility of the HIPed NiAl-Fe(Nb) alloy are higher than that of as- cast alloy, and the increase is large at low temperature.

evidence.section: Effect of process on tensile property
evidence.quote: because of solid solution strengthening and precipitate strengthenin g resulting from the addition of Nb element, the yield strength and ultimate strength of the NiAl-Fe (Nb) alloy are much higher than that of the Ni-20Al-30Fe-Y alloy[11] at the same processing and testing condition.

evidence.section: Effect of process on tensile property
evidence.quote: The yield strength and ultimate strength of the DS NiAl-Fe(Nb) alloy are equivalent to that of as-cast NiAl-Fe(Nb) alloy, but the elongation of the DS NiAl-Fe(Nb) alloy is the highest among the three processing alloys, and the elongation exceeds 100% at 1273K, i. e. the DS NiAl-Fe(Nb) alloy exhibits superplastic deformation behavior.
